title: Right now
description: Say what is happening at this moment.
grammarNote: The progressive is estar plus a gerund: estoy leyendo. An -ar verb makes -ando, an -er or -ir verb makes -iendo.

explanation.summary: The present progressive is for something that is happening now, or that is going on around you. It is estar plus a gerund, and the gerund is made by changing the ending of the infinitive.

sections.heading: Making the gerund
sections.body: An -ar verb drops the ar and adds ando: hablar becomes hablando. An -er or -ir verb drops the er or ir and adds iendo: comer becomes comiendo, vivir becomes viviendo. Ver becomes viendo, and the stem-changing verbs lose their change: dormir becomes durmiendo.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: The progressive says what is in progress: ahora estoy trabajando. It also covers the near future, because Spanish has no other way to say what you are about to do: estoy yendo, I am going. And it can be used for a routine that is happening now, like esta semana estoy viajando.

examples.en: I am going to the market.
This week I am on holiday.

sections.heading: With the word for right now
sections.body: The word ahora goes at the start or the end, and either is fine. But the verb comes before it when it is at the end: estoy trabajando ahora. And Spanish often adds the gerund with estar for something that is going on around you: está lloviendo, it is raining.

items.note: Feminine: la televisión. You watch it: ver la televisión.
Feminine: la música. It has no plural in everyday use.
Masculine: el partido. It also means a party.

drills.note: Dormir makes durmiendo and loses the stem change.
